page: Amazon Web Services c8gn.12xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by AWS Graviton processors. It features 48 dedicated physical cores on the arm64 architecture, utilizing the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 model running at 2.8 GHz. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 96.0 GB of memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 150 Gbps.

Benchmark results show strong multi-core and memory performance. The multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core scores rank in the top 25% and top 10% respectively, supported by top-tier multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and software compilation with Clang. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only and write large block tests reaching the top 10% tier. However, single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and Passmark CPU scores falling in the middle 50% average category.

This hardware profile is suited for network-intensive and compute-heavy workloads such as static web serving, where throughput benchmarks rank in the top 10%, and database operations, which also score in the top 10% tier. The 150 Gbps network baseline supports high-throughput data transfers. For machine learning, the instance demonstrates average prompt processing across various model sizes, though text generation with a small 135M model is weak, falling into the bottom 25%. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage.
